description.narrative: Kosovo has strengthened its waste management framework through Law No. 04/L 060 on Waste, amended in 2022 and 2024, to further align with the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC). These amendments reinforce key circular economy principles, including the waste hierarchy, the polluter pays principle, and extended producer responsibility.In early 2026, the Regional Waste Company“Pastrimi” (KRM “Pastrimi”) formally notified the Municipality of Pristinathat it lacks sufficient operational capacity, adequate mechanical equipment, and financial stability to fully addressthe city’s waste-management needs. This notification confirmed a service gap particularly affecting areas whereaccumulated waste poses environmental risks and public-health concerns, and underscored the need for immediatemunicipal intervention to maintain basic service standards. The Improved Waste Management and Collection Projecthas been developed in response to these gaps and aims to provide Pristina Municipality with reliable, continuouswaste-collection operations, secure transportation of waste to authorized disposal facilities, and strengthenedpublic-space cleanliness.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
